blocks.text: One disputed reading sees Hosea challenging the attribution of grain, wine, oil, fertility, and security to Baal or rival practices. The chapter’s images of failed harvest, lost fertility, and exile then sharpen its accusation of unfaithfulness. Yet these references should not be taken as evidence for one simple, uniform fertility cult; Hosea also recalls earlier traditions, including the wilderness, Gibeah, and Baal-peor, to diagnose Israel’s present identity.

sections.title: A Question of Loyalty and Provision
